Article Title: Jharkhand student protest Day 14: Hunger strike continues as BJP, Rahul Gandhi back students
Article Text:
Students protest in Ranchi's Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium.

BJP MLAs protest outside Assembly

Rahul Gandhi speaks to aspirants

11-member delegation finalised

Officials reach protest site

'Assembly gherao' on Monday

Minister claims 19 arrested

NEW DELHI: The protest by JPSC and JSSC aspirants in Jharkhand entered its 14th day on Thursday, with students demanding action over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations, while political pressure on the Hemant Soren government intensified.The protest, launched on July 25 under the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch at Ranchi's Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, has grown into one of Jharkhand’s largest student-led movements in recent years. Protesters are seeking cancellation of the 14th JPSC Civil Services Preliminary Examination, an independent probe into alleged irregularities, and comprehensive reforms in the JPSC and JSSC. Here are the top developments:BJP MLAs on Thursday staged a protest outside the Jharkhand Assembly, on the first day of the Monsoon Session, over alleged irregularities in the state competitive examinations.Speaking to ANI, BJP MLA Alok Chaurasia said, "The Bharatiya Janata Party stands firmly and vocally with the students regarding the functioning of Jharkhand government agencies such as JPSC, JSSC, and CJL, as well as the widespread corruption across the state, particularly the fraud committed against students..."The legislators raised slogans against the government, with chief whip Naveen Jaiswal alleging it was "selling" Jharkhand's youths' future and demanding a CBI probe, saying, "nobody trusts your CID and committee." Rahul Gandhi speaks to aspirantsCongress leader Rahul Gandhi spoke to JPSC-JSSC aspirants over the phone on Thursday. Student leader Piyush Kumar said the students raised their demand for cancellation of the examination, an investigation and reforms."We told him of our demands, that exam should be cancelled, regarding investigation and reforms. He said that he stands with our demands, and that they will take it up with the Govt. He said that he stands with and supports students...We are yet to get any official information regarding the date and time of meeting (with the government)," Kumar said.Student leader Ravindra Paswan said Gandhi enquired about the situation at the protest site."He asked us about the situation here. We told him about the irregularities in exams here. We told him that Congress is in the government in Jharkhand and they should help us. He told us that he stands with students," Paswan said.According to JPSC JSSC Reform Manch, protesting students have finalised an 11-member delegation for talks with the state government. The group comprises eight student representatives, one lawyer and two technical experts.The eight student representatives are Piyush Kumar Singh, Ravindra Paswan, Rajesh Prasad, Neetu Kujur, Kartik Soren, Ravindra, Ankit Kumar and Shalu Singh.Students have also demanded that any dialogue with the government be held in the presence of the media.Ranchi Sadar SDO Rajat Kumar and ADM Dhananjay Kumar reached Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium to hear the grievances of the protesting aspirants."We came to speak with our younger brothers about how we can assist them in their preparations for the future," Rajat Kumar said.A protester said there had been a suggestion that a four- or five-member delegation should participate in talks, but students insisted on a transparent process.Amid the continuing agitation, students announced a "Vidhan Sabha Gherao" on August 10 if their demands are not met. Protester Radhe Kumar said the decision was taken after the government initiated contact with the students.JMM MLA Jairam Kumar Mahato urged the government to immediately open talks, warning that "something untoward will happen" if the situation remains unresolved.Activist Sonam Wangchuk rejected reports that student leader Devendra Nath Mahato had ended his hunger strike after speaking with him. A total of six demonstrators are presently on a hunger strike.In a video message on X, Wangchuk said, "He consumed water, not food; I want to clarify this."He added, "He was fasting without water and without food, which is, in a way, like suicide. So, I only urged him to consume water and salt now and continue his fast."Mahato began his indefinite hunger strike on August 2 at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium. He is now continuing the fast on water and salt.Jharkhand minister Shilpi Neha Tirkey said on Thursday that the government was investigating the allegations and that 19 people had been arrested.
Article Summary: JPSC and JSSC aspirants in Jharkhand protest enters 14th day. Protesters seeking cancellation of 14th JPSC Civil Services Preliminary Examination. They also want independent probe into alleged irregularities, and comprehensive reforms.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi flags Ken-Betwa tribal displacement; Centre forwards complaints to MP govt
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi raises Ken-Betwa displacement issue

NEW DELHI: The Union ministry of tribal affairs on Thursday told the Lok Sabha that it has received several representations raising concerns over the displacement of people due to the Ken-Betwa river-link project in Madhya Pradesh.The ministry said it has forwarded the representations to the state government and the concerned district administrations for examination and appropriate action.In a written reply to questions from Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party MP Ajendra Singh Lodhi on the rehabilitation of tribal families affected by the project, compliance with the Forest Rights Act (FRA), and alleged evictions, the ministry said it had not received any complaints specifically claiming that compensation disbursed under the project had failed to reach beneficiaries.The ministry, however, said it had received representations "raising issues of displacement" due to the project.It added that the representations had been forwarded to the Madhya Pradesh government and the concerned district administrations for examination and appropriate action, while noting that the implementation of the Forest Rights Act (FRA) rests with state governments and Union Territory administrations.Minister of state for tribal affairs Durgadas Uikey, in his written reply, said the representations had been referred to the state authorities. "These have been forwarded to the State Government of Madhya Pradesh and respective District Administrations for examination and necessary action," the reply said.In its response, the ministry said the rehabilitation plan for Scheduled Tribe families affected by the Ken-Betwa river-link project was based on a proposal submitted by the National Water Development Agency in 2016.Citing the 2016 proposal, the ministry said the project's first phase is expected to displace 1,913 families comprising 8,339 people, including 648 Scheduled Tribe families.Responding to questions on gram sabha meetings under the Forest Rights Act (FRA), the ministry said it does not maintain centralised records of meeting dates, attendance, signatures, grievances related to consent, compensation and displacement, or the status of their disposal, as implementation of the law falls under the jurisdiction of state governments and Union Territory administrations.The ministry added that it has repeatedly urged states and UTs to ensure that no eligible beneficiary is denied forest rights and to strictly comply with Section 4(5) of the FRA, which prohibits the eviction or removal of claimants from forest land under their occupation until the process of recognition and verification of their rights has been completed.The Centre's response comes amid a prolonged protest by tribal families and other residents affected by the Ken-Betwa river-link project in Madhya Pradesh's Chhatarpur district over issues related to displacement, rehabilitation and resettlement.As part of the agitation, protesters staged a series of symbolic demonstrations in July, including a "jal satyagraha", "chita (pyre) satyagraha" and "faansi satyagraha".The protest also included an indefinite hunger strike by activist Amit Bhatnagar, who was later forcibly removed from the site by state police. Nearly 150 villagers were also removed during the operation, visuals of which drew nationwide attention.
Article Summary: The ministry said it has forwarded the representations to the state government and the concerned district administrations for examination and appropriate action. The Centre's response comes amid a prolonged protest by tribal families and other residents affected by the Ken-Betwa river-link project in Madhya Pradesh.

Article Title: Stalker uses husband's name to lure teacher to school gate, stabs her 20 times in Faridabad
Article Text:
Footage shows accused lunge at Sandhya the moment she reaches the classroom entrance, and pull her to the corridor

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think should be done to better prevent stalking-related crimes? Stricter laws against stalking Faster action on complaints More public awareness campaigns 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





GURGAON: A stalker who allegedly pursued a 26-year-old teacher for nearly two years walked into a private school in Faridabad on Monday morning, tricked her into coming to the main gate by using her husband’s name, and then stabbed her more than 20 times in a vicious attack in front of staff and students until the blade bent.Captured on CCTV cameras, the attack unfolded in seconds and left the young English teacher dead before she could be taken to hospital.The accused, Amit (21), a resident of Kot village in Faridabad, was arrested within a couple of hours. Police said he had been stalking Sandhya, who taught at Saraswati Senior Secondary School in Sikrona, and attacked her after she allegedly severed all contact with him and warned him she would approach police if he continued to harass her.Amit entered the school around 9.30am, his face partially covered with a scarf, and asked staff to inform Sandhya that “Vicky” had come to meet her, referring to her husband. Believing her husband was waiting outside, she walked towards the entrance.Footage shows him lunge at Sandhya the moment she reaches the classroom entrance, and pull her to the corridor. Amit punches her as she cries out for help, pulls out a knife in a flash and goes on a stabbing fit, puncturing her neck, abdomen and upper body several times as she slumps to the ground.School principal Tejpal is seen rushing into the corridor to rescue Sandhya after hearing her screams but is forced to step back as the attacker threatens him with the knife.“There were students inside the school and Sandhya was taking classes. He used her husband’s name to call her outside. No sooner did he reach the gate, he attacked her. He stabbed her over 20 times. When I tried to stop him, he threatened to attack me too. We rushed her to Al-Falah Medical College, where she was declared dead on arrival,” the principal told TOI.Police sources said Amit had allegedly bought the knife around two months ago and is suspected to have been planning the murder since then. While the exact number of stab wounds will be confirmed after the autopsy, CCTV footage showed him stabbing Sandhya about 20 times in just 13 seconds. Amit had come to the school on a motorcycle.Sandhya, who had a love marriage with Vikas, is survived by their two children — a five-year-old son and a three-year-old daughter. The attack triggered panic on the campus. Teachers quickly moved frightened children back into classrooms while parents began arriving after news spread. Police cordoned off the school as forensic teams collected evidence.Based on a complaint by Sandhya’s husband, a case was registered under Section 103(1) (murder) of BNS at Sector 58 police station.Police spokesperson Yashpal Yadav said the anti-vehicle theft squad and a team from Sikrona police station tracked down Amit within two hours.“During questioning, the accused said he knew Sandhya from the school in his village where she earlier taught. She later stopped speaking to him and warned of legal action if he continued following her,” Yadav added.Police said the accused will be produced before a local court and his custody sought for further interrogation. CCTV footage and other evidence are being examined as part of the probe, they added.
Article Summary: A stalker walked into a private school in Faridabad on Monday morning, tricked her into coming to the main gate by using her husband’s name. He then stabbed her more than 20 times in a vicious attack in front of staff and students until the blade bent. The accused, Amit (21), a resident of Kot village infaridabad, was arrested within a couple of hours.

Article Title: 'Arrest Abhijeet Dipke immediately': Social media influencer files complaint against CJP founder
Article Text:
Ansari alleged that men associated with Abhijeet Dipke attacked him and urged the police to arrest Dipke immediately.





NEW DELHI: Social media influencer Faizan Ansari on Tuesday said he has filed a written complaint with the Delhi Police against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke, alleging that men linked to the party attacked him in Maharashtra.Ansari claimed he has evidence to support his allegations and urged the police to arrest Dipke immediately."Today, I have filed a written complaint against Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the CJP party, with the Delhi DCP, because I have proof that his men attacked me. I was attacked in Pune and in Aurangabad. There are already 2 cases filed on that, " Ansari told ANI.He also praised the Delhi government and police for detaining activist Sonam Wangchuk during the recent protests, claiming the move prevented the law and order situation in the national capital from worsening."I want the Delhi police to immediately arrest Dipke. Moreover, I salute the Delhi CM and the police for detaining Sonam Wangchuk at the right time, due to which the atmosphere in Delhi was saved from deteriorating. Dipke is doing everything for his own benefit, " Ansari added“Moreover, I salute the Delhi CM and the police for detaining Sonam Wangchuk at the right time, due to which the atmosphere in Delhi was saved from deteriorating.Dipke is doing everything for his own benefit,” Ansari alleged.Earlier on Monday, Dipke had rejected comparisons between the CJP-led protests over alleged recruitment and examination irregularities and anti-government movements in Bangladesh and Nepal, saying Indian protesters draw inspiration from Mahatma Gandhi's legacy of peaceful resistance.Dipke also spoke about the CJP's expansion plans, compensation for the families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide, and the state of education in India.Dipke also dismissed exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen's remarks comparing the CJP's protest in Delhi against exam irregularities with the 2024 movement that led to the ouster of former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina's Awami League government.“Protests in Bangladesh, Nepal are being used to defame us; we are different," he asserted.“We showed during the recent protest in Delhi that we were following the Constitution and holding our demonstration peacefully. Parallels to the protests in Bangladesh and Nepal are being used to defame us.“We don’t need to look at Bangladesh or Nepal when we have Mahatma Gandhi from whom the world takes inspiration to protest,” Dipke said.People are drawing comparisons with the protests in Bangladesh and Nepal because the alleged police brutality reminded them of scenes from those countries, he said.“The students in India were not violent or aggressive. They got their heads, arms and legs broken but displayed restraint and sat peacefully at Jantar Mantar," Dipke said.
Article Summary: Social media influencer Faizan Ansari on Tuesday said he has filed a written complaint with the Delhi Police against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke. Ansari claimed he has evidence to support his allegations and urged the police to arrest Dipke immediately. He also praised the Delhi government and police for detaining activist Sonam Wangchuk.

Article Title: South Africa recalls envoy for attending Zuma meet with businessman Gupta
Article Text:
Gupta and his brothers are accused of political corruption and Zuma faced allegations of extending undue favour to them

NEW DELHI: The South African high commissioner to India, Anil Sooklal, is understood to have been recalled for attending a meeting between former president Jacob Zuma and an Indian-origin businessman facing charges of corruption in that country.South African foreign minister Ronald Lamola said Sooklal has been recalled for “consultations”. The move came after photographs emerged of Zuma and Sooklal meeting controversial businessman Ajay Gupta on June 26 in Haridwar.Gupta and his brothers are accused of political corruption, and Zuma faced allegations of extending undue favour to them when he was the South African president from 2009 to 2018. Zuma and the Gupta brothers rejected all allegations.The Gupta brothers left South Africa after Zuma lost power, when his party, the African National Congress, forced him to resign following allegations of corruption.
Article Summary: Anil Sooklal is understood to have been recalled for attending a meeting between former president Jacob Zuma and an Indian-origin businessman facing charges of corruption in that country. The move came after photographs emerged of Zuma. meeting controversial businessman Ajay Gupta on June 26 in Haridwar.

SRINAGAR: J&K Police registered an FIR against PDP ’s Iltija Mufti , accusing her of assaulting a police officer during the party’s protest against the abrogation of Article 370 on Tuesday, an officer said.Iltija has been booked under sections 121, 132 and 191 of BNS that relate to assaulting public servants and rioting. Article Title: Wangchuk gives government 1 month to drop cases, compensate kin of Leh protest firing victims
Article Text:
Sonam said the government has about one month to address these issues, otherwise they shall be compelled to launch another movement in Ladakh

SRINAGAR: Leh Apex Body functionaries Sonam Wangchuk and Chering Dorjay Lakrook gave Union government a one-month deadline to withdraw criminal cases against around 80 protesters charged during last year’s agitation for Sixth Schedule status and statehood for Ladakh, compensate families of four demonstrators killed in police firing, and provide relief to those seriously wounded, warning of a fresh movement if their demands remain unmet.“People in Ladakh are deeply hurt as four unarmed civilians lost their lives last year and dozens were wounded. We hope government will review what happened and provide compensation to the families of those killed (on Sept 24 last year in Leh) and withdraw all cases against those who were arrested and jailed,” Wangchuk said Thursday in Leh.“We are giving government about one month to address these issues. If it fails to do so, we will be compelled to launch another movement in Ladakh,” he said, adding Ladakh “should be governed with trust and respect, not fear”.Lakrook condemned the recent police action against NEET paper leak protesters at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi but called the crackdown in Leh far harsher. He alleged the response from media, people and political parties to the use of force in Ladakh was far weaker. “Every citizen deserves the same concern and justice, whether they live in Ladakh or elsewhere in India.”Lakrook said LAB and Kargil Democratic Alliance had pursued their four-point agenda for years, but talks with Centre had yielded little progress.“There has been some progress but there is still no decision on our core demands,” he said, describing Ladakh as a strategically sensitive region whose concerns should not be pushed to the back burner.After the firing on Sept 24, authorities imposed curfew-like restrictions, suspended mobile internet and arrested more than 70 people, including Wangchuk, who was accused of inciting protesters. Wangchuk was held under NSA in Jodhpur jail until Centre revoked his detention in March. Talks resumed after his release and he described the May 22 meeting with Centre as positive after it agreed to discuss Article 371-like protections for Ladakh.
Article Summary: Leh Apex Body functionaries Sonam Wangchuk and Chering Dorjay Lakrook gave Union government a one-month deadline to withdraw criminal cases against around 80 protesters charged during last year’s agitation for Sixth Schedule status and statehood for Ladakh. Warned of a fresh movement if their demands remain unmet.

Article Title: J&K CM visits flood-hit Rajouri, reviews relief measures
Article Text:
Jammu: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah inspects the flood affected areas to assess the damage caused, in Rajouri. (PTI Photo)

JAMMU: J&K CM Omar Abdullah visited flood-hit Rajouri district Thursday to assess the destruction caused by last month’s rain fury. He directed authorities concerned to expedite restoration works, intensify relief and rehabilitation efforts, and adopt long-term mitigation measures to safeguard vulnerable areas.Recognising that the existing relief structure was inadequate to cover reconstruction and rehabilitation costs, the CM assured citizens that the government would enhance the quantum of relief and provide comprehensive rehabilitation assistance to families whose houses were damaged and those rendered landless.Families who lost their homes as well as agricultural land will be provided five marlas (around 1,361.2sqft) for rehabilitation, said Omar, directing Rajouri deputy commissioner to identify suitable government land for the purpose. He also ordered the administration to arrange special free ration for such households.Omar said construction along vulnerable riverbanks would not be permitted, noting that rivers reclaim their natural courses during extreme weather events. Noting that the 33kV power transmission line between Rajouri and Poonch had suffered extensive damage, disrupting electricity supply, the CM ordered the power department to complete permanent restoration at the earliest. He also told PWD to recommend disaster-resistant solutions for hilly roads requiring resilient engineering designs suited to mountainous terrain.
Article Summary: J&K CM Omar Abdullah visited flood-hit Rajouri district Thursday to assess the destruction caused by last month's rain fury. He directed authorities concerned to expedite restoration works, intensify relief and rehabilitation efforts, and adopt long-term mitigation measures to safeguard vulnerable areas.

Article Title: BJP distances itself from ‘anti-women’ slogans at 370 event
Article Text:
Some BJP workers began raising anti-women slogans during 7th anniversary “celebrations” of Article 370’s abrogation

SRINAGAR: BJP distanced itself Thursday from slogans raised by some of its workers during “celebrations” marking the seventh anniversary of Article 370’s abrogation the previous day after backlash over their alleged anti-women content.“The party firmly believes in respecting the dignity of women and remains committed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of women empowerment. BJP has been at the forefront of empowering women and the historic decision to provide 33% reservation for women reflects that commitment,” BJP general secretary (organisation) Ashok Koul said.During Wednesday’s event in south Kashmir’s Anantnag, the BJP workers altered a well-known slogan of J&K’s governing National Conference (NC) associated with Article 370. For decades, the NC slogan has been “...Aze hund izat te Faze hund izat 370 (the honour of Azi and Fazi is Article 370)”. Azi and Fazi are names of women in the Valley.The BJP workers modified the slogan to “...Moklev Fazi hund te Azi hund izat (the honour of Fazi and Azi has ended)”. This ran counter to the NC slogan’s emphasis on dignity and respect in its discourse on Article 370.Images of BJP workers dancing to these slogans evoked sharp social media criticism with people decrying them as derogatory to women, forcing the party to issue the clarification.“Some individuals may have raised slogans based on their personal thinking or emotions, but those slogans do not represent BJP’s official stand or the views of the leaders who led the rally. The party does not endorse any defamatory or derogatory remarks against anyone,” BJP spokesperson Altaf Thakur said.Rivals were not convinced. “Some insults are not directed at individuals but at an entire society. Azi and Fazi are not merely names. They symbolise the respect, affection and dignity with which Kashmir has always regarded its mothers and sisters. The day they chose to turn those names into a joke, they crossed a line,” NC spokesperson Tanvir Sadiq said.PDP spokesperson Syed Tajamul Islam echoed the sentiment. “Ideological differences are a natural part of public life. But there are certain boundaries that should never be crossed. Fazi and Azi symbolise our mothers. Regardless of political ambition, personal interests, or ideological beliefs, no one should insult, ridicule, or demean what they represent,” Islam said.
Article Summary: Some BJP workers began raising anti-women slogans during 7th anniversary ‘celebrations’ of Article 370’s abrogation the previous day. Images of BJP workers dancing to these slogans evoked sharp social media criticism with people decrying them as derogatory to women.

NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has filed a charge sheet against 11 accused in connection with the murder of Chandranath Rath, a close aide of West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, news agency PTI reported citing officials on Thursday.This comes days after the CBI arrested brothers Sagar Sonkar and Sahib Sonkar in connection with the murder.Investigators have alleged that Sagar, who previously worked with Rath, acted as a key conspirator by arranging the contract killing and funding the shooters.The agency is also probing his alleged links with a functionary of a rival political party after call records reportedly showed repeated contact with a local party office.Rath, a close aide and personal assistant to Adhikari, was shot dead by motorcycle-borne assailants on May 6, two days after the Assembly election results.The CBI has alleged the conspiracy had been in the works since December 2025 and has so far arrested multiple alleged shooters and intermediaries in the case.

Article Title: 'Celebrate handloom day like you marked friendship day': PM Modi's appeal in another Insta video
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday urged people to celebrate National Handloom Day with the same enthusiasm they showed for Friendship Day.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday urged people to celebrate National Handloom Day with the same enthusiasm they showed for Friendship Day, making a heartfelt appeal in yet another Instagram video aimed at connecting directly with Gen Z.In the video, PM Modi said that just as people enthusiastically exchanged friendship bands and celebrated their bonds with loved ones, they should now come together to honour India's rich handloom tradition. He encouraged citizens to buy and wear handloom products, saying that every purchase strengthens the livelihoods of lakhs of weavers while preserving the country's centuries-old cultural heritage."Just as you celebrated Friendship Day with great warmth, celebrate Handloom Day too," the PM said, urging people to make handloom a part of their daily lives rather than limiting it to a symbolic occasion. He noted that every handloom product carries with it the story of an artisan's hard work, skill and dedication.PM Modi also highlighted the role of India's weaving community in keeping traditional crafts alive across generations. He said that choosing handloom products is not merely a matter of fashion but also a way of supporting the country's artisans and promoting the spirit of 'Vocal for Local'.The appeal comes ahead of National Handloom Day, observed annually on August 7 to commemorate the launch of the Swadeshi Movement in 1905 and to recognise the contribution of India's handloom sector to the country's cultural and economic fabric. The Centre has been marking the day since 2015 through various initiatives aimed at promoting indigenous textiles and encouraging consumers to support local weavers.The Instagram video is the latest in a series of direct-to-camera messages posted by the Prime Minister on social media, a format that has drawn significant public attention in recent weeks.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi on Thursday urged people to celebrate National Handloom Day with the same enthusiasm they showed for Friendship Day. He encouraged citizens to buy and wear handloom products, saying that every purchase strengthens the livelihoods of lakhs of weavers.

Article Title: Gen Z more honest, protesters not anti-national: Bhagwat
Article Text:
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat at an interaction with 'Gen Z' in Mumbai

NEW DELHI: Calling Gen Z and Gen Alpha more "honest" than adults RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Thursday rejected attempts to brand protesting youngsters "anti-national," and said they have "an honest feeling of patriotism." He described protest as a legitimate form of democratic dialogue and said their questions must be answered with logic, affection and a sense of belonging.By the end of the freewheeling exchange, the 75-year-old had also picked up a new expression from his young audience — “clock it” — and tried it out before the cheering crowd, adding a lighter finish to a conversation that ranged from student protests and reservation to social media, LGBTQ rights and relations with Pakistan and China.The interaction, held as part of IIMUN’s 15th anniversary celebration in Mumbai, was driven by questions from Gen Z and Gen Alpha delegates on issues ranging from education and jobs to reservation, social media and the right to protest.“I feel that this new generation — Gen Z and Gen Alpha — is more honest than our existing generation. There is an honest feeling of patriotism and service in them,” Bhagwat said, adding, “They are not anti-national.They are our own people, our next generation,” . The exchange came against the backdrop of recent Gen Z-led protests over examination irregularities, education and jobs.Bhagwat said young people today were unlike earlier generations that often accepted what elders told them without question. “They ask questions. They want logical answers, and along with that, they want affection,” he said.“I feel this new generation — Gen Z and Gen Alpha — is more honest than our existing generation. The honest impulse of patriotism and service is stronger in them,” he added.Bhagwat said protest should not be treated as the opposite of dialogue. “Protest is also a way of dialogue,” he said, describing it as a democratic means of building consensus. An agitation, he added, should seek to correct the system rather than target individuals or deepen divisions.Asked about allegations of lathi-charge and pellet firing on young protesters, Bhagwat said he did not have enough verified information to reach a conclusion. “I place my trust in Gen Z,” he said.Bhagwat backed the longstanding demand to allocate 6% of the Budget to education, saying, “The demand is justified. It should be implemented.” He also argued that education should not be treated as a commercial business.Turning to social media, Bhagwat warned against trusting content without checking authentic sources, particularly when technology could produce fake images, voices and videos. Influencers and public figures, he said, must recognise their responsibility because lakhs of people may imitate them.Turning to affirmative action, he said reservation must continue as long as social discrimination remained. “Those who have received its benefit and whose condition has improved should give up that benefit for others,” he said. Bhagwat also referred favourably to sub-categorisation so that the benefits reached those still left behind, and blamed politics for creating “bad blood” over a measure intended to promote social unity.The discussion also moved to LGBTQ rights. Bhagwat said the community was part of society and must be accommodated, but favoured wider debate on a legal framework for same-sex companionship rather than an immediate change to the institution of marriage.He also said people-to-people relations with Pakistan and China could be paused during war or terrorism but should not be permanently severed. “Permanent enmity is not the solution,” he said.The discussion also turned to jobs, with Bhagwat arguing that employment should not be reduced to salaried or government work. Entrepreneurship, skilled work and self-employment were equally valid, he said, calling for the restoration of "shram pratishtha", or dignity of labour. Society, he added, must stop ranking occupations as high or low and accord equal respect to anyone earning honestly, whether through farming, manual work, private employment, government service or a small enterprise.Asked why the RSS remained a male organisation despite describing women as equal partners in nation-building, Bhagwat said men and women were “equal and complementary” and should receive the same training and opportunities. He said the Rashtra Sevika Samiti functioned independently with the RSS’s support, while women working in public organisations were invited to the Akhil Bharatiya Pratinidhi Sabha and participated in its decision-making process. He also indicated that organisational integration could be considered if the women’s organisation itself sought it.
Article Summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat rejects attempts to brand protesting youngsters 'anti- national' He described protest as a legitimate form of democratic dialogue and said their questions must be answered with logic, affection and a sense of belonging. The interaction was held as part of IIMUN’s 15th anniversary celebration.

Article Title: ‘Will be a pressure group’: CJP announces nationwide 'Kya Bolti Public' campaign from September

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) said on Thursday that they will continue to function as a public pressure group instead of entering electoral politics for now, after a two-day meeting of the organisation's core team in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.Addressing a press conference after the meeting, its founder Abijeet Dipke said CJP would focus on building a nationwide citizens' movement around issues including unemployment, education, transparency, accountability and institutional reforms. In this context, they announced a "Kya Bolti Public" campaign.The campaign will involve CJP representatives across the country to seek people's views on the issues they face and understand what they think about the present political and social situation. “During the ‘Kya Bolti Public’ campaign, we will get to know what people think of the present situation in the country and what the issues they face are,” he said."For now, CJP will be a pressure group because what India needs right now is a pressure group," he clarified.He said the organisation's work would extend beyond education-related issues and focus on wider concerns around governance and democratic institutions."Whether it is the political system, the judiciary, the media, or the Election Commission, the reality is that people have lost faith in all these institutions," Dipke said.He added that CJP wanted to build public pressure to restore accountability and neutrality in these institutions, adding that "the political system today, in my opinion, is in a very bad state".Unemployment is another issue the organisation plans to take up nationally. "Unemployment is a major problem, we will make it a nationwide issue," Dipke said.He also said CJP would work on education reforms and criticised the rising cost of education. "Education has remained unaffordable since schooling. Education is used for making profits. But we want to change it," he said.Dipke further stated that young people would be a key focus of the nationwide campaign, noting that 60 per cent of India's population is below the age of 35. He said unemployed youngsters had also participated in CJP's protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi last month.The organisation had led protests over the NEET paper leak and other alleged examination irregularities. Dipke described the resignation of former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan as a major outcome of the agitation. "Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation is the biggest achievement of the students' agitation," he said.The two-day core committee meeting also focused on expanding CJP's grassroots presence across states, strengthening its organisational network and preparing for the nationwide youth outreach campaign.Dipke rejected speculation that CJP was preparing to enter electoral politics, saying the organisation had no immediate plans to become a political party. Instead, it would seek to build a nationwide citizens' movement around transparency, accountability and institutional reforms.He also expressed support for students protesting over alleged examination irregularities in Jharkhand and said CJP members, including its leadership, could visit the state if required.The CJP founder also called for efforts to restore the credibility of the media, making it another focus of the organisation's broader campaign.
Article Summary: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) said on Thursday that they will continue to function as a public pressure group instead of entering electoral politics. Its founder Abijeet Dipke said CJP would focus on building a nationwide citizens' movement around issues including unemployment, education, transparency and accountability.

Article Title: 'Hemant Soren unfit to hold office': Jharkhand students on hunger strike demand CM's resignation

NEW DELHI: Students protesting in Jharkhand over the irregularities in the government-job recruitment process have grown livid over the state dispensation's inability to address the issue swiftly and efficiently.One of the several students on hunger strike lashed out at chief minister Hemant Soren for not visiting the protest site and called the JMM supremo "unfit to hold" the hightest office in the state, demanding his resignation.Gearing up for assembly "gherao" on August 10 in the backdrop of the ineffective redressal, a protester said: "We remain steadfast until the government accepts our demands. However, judging by the government's actions and what we are hearing through the media, it still does not appear to be taking a positive approach toward our demands. This government has eyes, ears and sensitivity. Whatever is appropriate and in the interest of students, the state government will decide accordingly," he added.The chief minister said investigations into the allegations were under way and that the government would take a decision after receiving reports from the agencies probing the matter.

Article Title: 'Convey sentiments': Rajya Sabha Chairman tells Kiren Rijiju after opposition demands Amit Shah's presence
Article Text:
Rajya Sabha witnessed multiple adjournments during the day as opposition members continued sloganeering and asking for the presence of Amit Shah. (Photo: PTI)

NEW DELHI: Parliament proceedings remained disrupted on Thursday as opposition parties continued to demand the presence of Union home minister Amit Shah over the police action against student protesters at Jantar Mantar. The Lok Sabha was also repeatedly adjourned amid the continued uproar.Amid the repeated disruptions, Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan asked Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju to "echo the sentiments" and demand to the home minister.As the Rajya Sabha reassembled, the Chairman attempted to take up the Question Hour, but opposition members continued sloganeering. He repeatedly urged protesting MPs to maintain order and assured them they would get an opportunity to raise their concerns.The Chair then allowed leader of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge to speak. However, members of the Treasury benches objected, triggering a heated exchange between the ruling and opposition members.Kharge reiterated the opposition's demand that Amit Shah address the House on the police action against protesters and said the opposition was ready for a discussion."We only raise genuine questions concerning the country and its 140 crore people.We are asking the Home Minister and the Prime Minister to come to the House. We request the Chair to direct the Home Minister to come and give a statement. We are ready to discuss it," Kharge later posted on X."In this very House, Arun Jaitley ji himself said that disruption is a part of Parliamentary Democracy. You can raise any questions that is relevant to the proceedings. But here, when we are asking genuine questions, they are escaping," he added.Responding to the demand, Rijiju said Kharge had not cited any rule while making the request and could not decide which minister should reply on behalf of the government."The leader of the opposition did not quote any rule, cannot give direction to the Chair, only make requests, cannot dictate. New Congress members not learning anything because their leadership not giving them a chance", Rijiju told Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge in Rajya Sabha.Following the exchange, the Rajya Sabha Chairman directed Rijiju to convey the sentiments of the opposition to the home minister."Now i request you to consider his request. Kharge requested the presence of home minister in the house. You represent him. As a parliamentary affairs minister you can echo the sentiments to the home minister," the RS Chairman said.Outside Parliament, Kharge said the Chairman had asked the Parliamentary affairs minister to ensure Amit Shah came to the House and made a statement."This is a simple request, and it is well within the government's control. Why they are not present is still unknown. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha told the Parliamentary affairs minister that the home minister should come to the House and speak on this incident. Rijiju alone does not have the authority to resolve the issue. He only conveys the matter, and then the issue fizzles out," Kharge said."When I raise a point of order, I am not allowed to speak. We want the House to run peacefully, and for that, the Home Minister should make a statement in the House. Instead of asking students to seek forgiveness, the government should apologise to the students and their families," he added.Asked whether the opposition would continue its protest, Kharge said the next course of action would depend on the government's response."It depends on when the Home Minister comes to the House and what statement he makes. Even the Prime Minister should come to the House and apologise. Such a serious incident has taken place, and yet the Home Minister has not made a statement," he said."We are raising the students' cause. We have written to our allies as well. Wherever there is an issue concerning students, we will raise it and stand with them," he added.The Rajya Sabha witnessed multiple adjournments during the day as opposition members continued sloganeering. Proceedings were first adjourned within 30 minutes of the House assembling, and later again till 2.15 pm and subsequently 3.15 pm with normal business repeatedly disrupted.
Article Summary: The Rajya Sabha witnessed multiple adjournments during the day as opposition members continued sloganeering. The Lok Sabha was also repeatedly adjourned amid the continued uproar. Opposition parties continued to demand the presence of Union home minister Amit Shah over the police action against student protesters at Jantar Mantar.

Article Title: Soaked in rain, fired by anger: JPSC-JSSC aspirants & students' Tiranga march rocks Ranchi
Article Text:
Holding the Tricolour aloft and carrying what organisers described as an approximately 600-metre-long national flag, the students marched through Ranchi.

As the march drew to a close, the rain intensified, but so did chants of "Jai Jharkhand".

RANCHI: Undeterred by relentless rain, hundreds of students gathered at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in Ranchi on Wednesday before setting out on a Tiranga March to Albert Ekka Chowk, intensifying an agitation that has entered its second week over alleged irregularities in Jharkhand's recruitment examinations.The march came amid an indefinite protest by students demanding a CBI investigation into the alleged paper leaks and recruitment irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) examinations.The movement has also escalated on the hunger strike front. Alongside Devendra Nath Mahto, dubbed by protesters as "Sonam Wangchuk 2.0", four more students have joined an indefinite fast, pressing three principal demands: cancellation of all JPSC and JSSC examinations conducted during the Hemant Soren-led JMM government's tenure; a CBI probe into the alleged irregularities, paper leaks and delays in recruitment results instead of an investigation by the state's Criminal Investigation Department (CID), which the students say they no longer trust; and comprehensive reforms to Jharkhand's recruitment and competitive examination system.The Tiranga March began with chants of "Jai Jharkhand" and slogans celebrating student unity. Organisers repeatedly instructed participants to refrain from using abusive language in slogans or on placards, stressing that the protest would remain peaceful and disciplined.The emphasis on restraint reflected the students' attempt to draw a clear distinction between their movement and political organisations.Protesters pointed out that two separate demonstrations have been taking place in Ranchi: one led by students and another believed to be backed by local MLA Jairam Singh Mahato's party. Organisers also appeared mindful of the aftermath of the recent Jantar Mantar protest in New Delhi, where FIRs and complaints were lodged against some protesters over the use of profanities. Students said they were determined to ensure that no such controversy overshadowed their movement.Holding the Tricolour aloft and carrying what organisers described as an approximately 600-metre-long national flag, the students marched through Ranchi despite the downpour."Our flag march represents the moral spirit of India. It highlights our constitutional rights. Look at all these students getting drenched in the rain while waving the Tricolour. This is a symbol of our unity and a symbol of our constitutional rights," one protester said.As the march reached Albert Ekka Chowk, groups of students gathered at the intersection and continued raising slogans. Traffic disruption remained limited, largely because authorities had already closed one of the approach roads. Protesters also allowed vehicles to pass intermittently, saying they did not want to cause unnecessary inconvenience to commuters.Appealing directly to the Hemant Soren government, another protester said, "We are the children of Jharkhand. You speak about working for the indigenous and tribal communities. Please work in our interest too. Thousands of students are studying with the hope of securing jobs in their own state. We request the government to reform the JPSC and JSSC."Several protesters contrasted the Ranchi agitation with the earlier demonstrations at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, insisting that their movement had remained peaceful throughout. They also warned that any police action, including a possible lathicharge, would only intensify the agitation."We are protesting peacefully. If the police take action against us, it will only raise questions about the government's role because we have not indulged in any violence. Every evening we gather at our protest site and peacefully put forward our demands," one participant said.As the march drew to a close, the rain intensified, but so did chants of "Jai Jharkhand". Some protesters invoked the state's historical icons while asserting that Jharkhand's identity extended beyond sporting achievements."Our identity is not defined by MS Dhoni. Our identity is defined by Birsa Munda, Tilka Manjhi, Shibu Soren, Binod Bihari Mahto, Bisheshwar Prasad Keshari, Sidhu and Kanhu," a protester said.Meanwhile, the Hemant Soren government has constituted a committee of ministers and senior officials to initiate talks with the agitating students. State minister Rajat said complaints regarding recruitment examination irregularities were already under investigation and that the agencies concerned were working on them with urgency.The students, however, rejected the proposal for closed-door discussions. They insisted that any dialogue with the government must be conducted transparently, in the presence of the media and television cameras, arguing that only an open process would inspire confidence among the protesters.
Article Summary: Hundreds of students march through Ranchi, intensifying agitation. They are demanding a CBI investigation into the alleged paper leaks and recruitment irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) The movement has also escalated on the hunger strike front. Four more students have joined an indefinite fast.

Article Title: 'Not fluent in Tamil is an insult': Actor Dhanush pushes for mother tongue first
Article Text:
Dhanush's strong pitch for Tamil

NEW DELHI: Actor Dhanush has renewed the focus on the language debate with his remarks stressing the importance of learning Tamil and being "fluent in one's mother tongue."Speaking at an event, the actor strongly backed the Tamil language and urged people to prioritise fluency in their mother tongue.Recalling his school days, Dhanush said, "When I was in school, we were fluent in Tamil and we struggled with English. Now the situation is opposite."He added, "Now, out of the 10 people I meet, eight don't know Tamil. One should be fluent in their mother tongue before everything else. To say I'm not fluent in Tamil is not a matter of pride. It's an insult. Focus on learning Tamil language."His remarks come amid the long-running language debate in Tamil Nadu, where the issue has frequently put the state government at odds with the Centre. Leaders across the state's political spectrum, from DMK chief and former CM MK Stalin to TVK founder and CM Vijay, have repeatedly accused the Centre of attempting to impose Hindi on southern states.
Article Summary: Actor Dhanush has urged people to prioritise fluency in their mother tongue. His remarks come amid the long-running language debate in Tamil Nadu. Leaders across the state's political spectrum have repeatedly accused the Centre of attempting to impose Hindi on southern states.

Article Title: Nagpur rape accused planned teen’s captivity, wants pizza, soft bedding & VIP comfort in police lock-up
Article Text:
A 20-year-old BBA student faces abduction and sexual assault charges. He is demanding luxury amenities and refusing police questioning.





NAGPUR: The 20-year-old BBA student, arrested in the alleged abduction and sexual assault of a 16-year-old girl, has begun complaining about dingy walls and a stinking toilet in lock-up and demanded pizza for breakfast and premium food for dinner. He is also refusing custodial interrogation after his top lawyer alleged police highhandedness in court on Tuesday, leaving cops in a fix.The accused, who refused medical examination and treatment, also refused to share his cell phone password and the survivor’s mobile, which he took control of during her 24-hour captivity. Sources at Hudkeshwar police station said the youth has been deftly stonewalling queries even as cops struggled to gather digital evidence. He was forcibly taken for medical examination on Tuesday.“The accused has been keeping the lock-up staff on their toes with repeated demands for VIP treatment. He has also been grumbling about sleepless nights, mosquito bites and demanded a thick cushion or a soft bedding and immediate installation of insect repellents in the lock-up,” said a senior official.Police sources said the accused has also been arguing with officers round the clock and has been pinning the blame on the 16-year-old girl for his sexual exploits.On Tuesday, the accused had levelled serious allegations against police before the special judge, alleging that police stole Rs 70,000 in cash from his rented flat, thrashed him and refused to return his spectacles and shoes. Police officers told TOI the youth is trying to inflict injuries on himself to strengthen the false narrative.Senior inspector Anamika Mirzapure of Hudkeshwar police station stated they have cooperated with the accused and met his basic needs. “If any accused demands luxury, soft beds, better food, and constantly argues, we cannot help. The accused is stalling interrogations and refusing to cooperate. We are constantly counselling him,” she said. Hassled policemen are monitoring him to prevent any self-harm attempts while continuing efforts to extract information.
Article Summary: BBA student arrested in alleged abduction and sexual assault of a 16-year-old girl. He has demanded pizza for breakfast and premium food for dinner. He is refusing custodial interrogation after his top lawyer alleged police highhandedness in court on Tuesday.
